nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $L$ a list of natural numbers and $w$ a list of bits. The occurrence table of the list $n$ followed by $L$, with $w$, is the entry whose name is the binary code of $n$ and whose value is the first bit of $w$ (no value if $w$ is empty), followed by the occurrence table of $L$ with $w$ minus its first bit (with the empty list if $w$ is empty).
nodes.title: Occurrence table of a nonempty list

nodes.summary: Let $w$, $t$, $b$ be lists of symbols, $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and $v$ a bit. In exactly one step, the SAT tokenizer goes from the label $\mathsf{fin}$ with internal bit $v$, empty formula stack $X$, stacks $W$, $T$, $B$ holding $w$, $t$, $b$, and $i$ and $j$ marks on the clause and literal counters, to the label $\mathsf{acc}$ with internal bit false and all stacks unchanged.

nodes.summary: The alphabet $G$ of the host's input stack is the pair alphabet $\mathrm{Bool} \oplus \mathrm{Option}\ \mathrm{Bool}$ of the dense SAT verifier.
nodes.title: Input alphabet of the SAT verifier host

nodes.summary: Each stack of the SAT verifier host has an alphabet: the input stack has the input alphabet $G$, the output stack has alphabet $\mathrm{Bool}$, and every other stack has the token alphabet $\mathrm{Sym}$.
nodes.title: Stack alphabets of the SAT verifier host

nodes.summary: The SAT verifier host has seventeen stacks: the input stack, the output stack, and fifteen work stacks, namely two holding the formula bits and the certificate bits, two scratch stacks used to move them in phase 0, the token and table stacks, six further stacks of the clause-check driver, two further stacks of the tokenizer, and one further stack of the 3-clause filter.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
